title: Value-Based Objection Handling
summary: When a buyer says the price is too high, clarify the business outcome and quantify the cost of the current problem before discussing concessions.
guidance: Use a value hypothesis, payback estimate, and success metric. Treat discounting as a later commercial option, not the first response.

title: Technical Proof for Implementation Risk
summary: Technical stakeholders need evidence that the proposed workflow can integrate with current systems and be delivered in manageable stages.
guidance: Use a focused proof, integration boundary map, sandbox demo, or phased rollout plan to reduce uncertainty.

title: Security and Compliance Discovery
summary: Security objections are often a decision gate rather than a generic request for documentation.
guidance: Map the security stakeholder, required evidence, data handling questions, audit controls, and approval sequence early in the deal.

title: Competitive Displacement
summary: Competitive deals are won by connecting incumbent gaps to measurable customer outcomes, not by listing more features.
guidance: Document the status quo cost, define a differentiated outcome, and give the executive sponsor a clear reason to change.

title: Stakeholder Change Management
summary: A champion change can reset the business case and remove momentum from an otherwise healthy evaluation.
guidance: Re-qualify the new stakeholder, rebuild the success criteria, and maintain a multi-threaded mutual action plan.
